stemMd: In a parallel axonometric projection, two distinct spatial lines are parallel and neither is viewed end-on. What is true of their projected directions?

options.label: B
options.textMd: Their angle equals their distance apart

options.label: E
options.textMd: They must meet at a finite vanishing point

explanationMd: A linear parallel projection maps equal direction vectors to equal image directions. Thus the lines remain parallel, although projection can place them on the same image line. The end-on exception is explicitly excluded.

distractorRationale.e: Finite convergence belongs to perspective rather than parallel projection.
distractorRationale.c: Parallel projection does not impose right angles.
distractorRationale.d: Straight lines remain straight or collapse.
distractorRationale.b: Angle and distance are different geometric quantities.
